1.q: [Week 1] According to the ITU Internet Report 2005 discussed in the lecture, the future Internet is expected to become wider and more complex mainly because:
options: Humans will completely stop using the Internet
Most Internet traffic may flow between devices and different kinds of things
Only desktop computers will remain connected
Internet communication will be restricted to email services
1.solution: The ITU report describes a future where humans may become a minority as generators and receivers of traffic. Instead, communication will increasingly happen between devices and “things,” forming the Internet of Things. See lecture 1 Introduction to IoT — Part-I @ 03:10

1.q: [Week 1] Which of the following are characteristics of IoT systems?
options: Presence of sleeping nodes, mobile nodes, and non-IP devices
Guaranteed continuous connectivity for every device at all times
1.solution: IoT systems require scalable architecture, clear naming and addressing, and must support heterogeneous devices such as sleeping nodes, mobile nodes, and non-IP devices. However, IoT systems may have intermittent connectivity, so option d is incorrect. See lecture 1: Introduction to IoT — Part-I @ 06:05

1.q: [Week 1] In the lecture, “Smart Dust” refers to:
options: A cloud storage model for IoT data
A large-scale wireless router used in smart cities
Very tiny computing devices that can be sprayed or injected for sensing purposes
A type of IPv6 address used in IoT networks
1.solution: Smart Dust refers to extremely small computing devices, smaller than a grain of sand, that can be used to measure chemicals in soil or diagnose problems in the human body. See lecture 1 Introduction to IoT — Part-I @ 10:40

1.q: [Week 1] Which statement best explains the relation between IoT and M2M communication?
options: IoT and M2M are exactly the same
M2M is broader than IoT because it includes people and applications
M2M is a part of IoT, while IoT has a broader scope of interactions
IoT does not include machine-to-machine interaction
1.solution: M2M focuses mainly on communication among machines and devices. IoT is broader because it includes interactions between things, people, applications, and systems. See lecture 1 Introduction to IoT — Part-I @ 19:30

1.q: [Week 1] State whether the following statement is True or False. Statement: In the Web of Things, IoT sensors are replaced completely by cloud databases.
1.solution: The Web of Things does not replace sensors. Sensors remain responsible for collecting physical-world data, while web technologies help expose and access IoT resources. See lecture 1 Introduction to IoT — Part-I @ 22:50

1.q: [Week 1] In an IoT network configuration, local addresses may be valid only within a gateway’s domain. The same local address may even appear under another gateway. The main advantage of this strategy is:
options: It removes the requirement of a gateway
It prevents any device from communicating with the Internet
1.solution: Using locally valid addresses within a gateway’s domain allows address reuse across different gateway domains. This helps avoid unnecessary wastage of global addresses. See lecture 2 Introduction to IoT — Part-II @ 05:30

1.q: [Week 1] Which of the following functions are associated with IoT gateways in the addressing strategy discussed in the lecture?
options: Obtaining upstream address prefixes using mechanisms such as DHCPv6
Delegating addresses to nodes using SLAAC
1.solution: IoT gateways can provide Internet connectivity and IoT LAN intra-connectivity. They may obtain upstream prefixes through DHCPv6 and delegate them to nodes using SLAAC. See lecture 2 Introduction to IoT — Part-II @ 09:40

1.q: [Week 1] Which of the following is true about IPv6 compared to IPv4?
options: IPv6 has a smaller address space than IPv4
IPv6 uses hexadecimal notation and supports a much larger address space
IPv6 requires broadcast addresses in the same way as IPv4
1.solution: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses and dotted decimal notation, whereas IPv6 uses 128- bit addresses and hexadecimal notation. This makes IPv6 more suitable for large-scale IoT addressing. See lecture 2 Introduction to IoT — Part-II @ 16:50

1.q: [Week 1] Which statement correctly represents the design expectation from a good sensor?
options: It should influence the measured property significantly
It should respond strongly to unrelated physical properties
It should be sensitive to the measured property and should not disturb it
It should always produce random output
1.solution: A good sensor should measure the desired property, remain insensitive to unrelated properties, and should not influence or alter the measured quantity. See lecture 3 Sensing @ 13:00

1.q: [Week 1] Which of the following statements about sensor resolution are correct?
options: Sensor resolution is the smallest change that the sensor can detect
For a digital sensor, resolution is related to the smallest digital output change it can process
Sensor resolution and sensor accuracy always refer to exactly the same property
Sensor accuracy does not depend only on resolution
1.solution: Resolution refers to the smallest detectable change in the measured quantity. In digital sensors, it is related to the smallest digital output step. However, accuracy and resolution are not the same; a high-resolution sensor may still be inaccurate if it has bias or calibration errors. See lecture 3 Sensing @ 14:10

1.q: [Week 1] State True or False. An accelerometer that measures acceleration along the x, y, and z coordinate axes is classified as a vector sensor.
1.solution: A vector sensor measures quantities that have both magnitude and direction or orientation. Since an accelerometer measures acceleration components along different coordinate axes, such as x, y, and z, it is classified as a vector sensor. See lecture 3 Sensing @ 18:40

1.q: [Week 1] A sensor gives different output for the same input value depending on whether that input was reached by increasing or decreasing the measured quantity. This error is called:
1.solution: Hysteresis error occurs when the sensor output depends on the previous input history. The same present input may give different readings depending on whether the input was approached from a lower or higher value. See lecture 3 Sensing @ 22:40

1.q: [Week 1] State True or False A hydraulic actuator can produce considerable force because liquids are nearly incompressible.
1.solution: A hydraulic actuator uses hydraulic fluid to generate mechanical motion. Since liquids are nearly incompressible, hydraulic actuators can exert large forces. See lecture 4 Actuation @ 06:20

1.q: [Week 1] Which of the following statements are correct about Shape Memory Polymer actuators?
options: They may respond to stimuli such as light, heat, electrical, magnetic, pH, or moisture changes
They can show high strain recovery
They may have properties such as low density and biocompatibility
They are used only as passive temperature sensors
1.solution: Shape Memory Polymer actuators can respond to different stimuli and are known for features such as low density, high strain recovery, biocompatibility, and biodegradability. They are actuator materials, not merely passive temperature sensors. See lecture 4 Actuation @ 18:20

1.q: [Week 1] State whether the following statement is True or False. Statement: According to the IoT implementation example discussed in the lecture, data gathered by a sensor travels through a gateway and a proxy server before arriving at the cloud server.
1.solution: In the example IoT implementation, the sensor first collects the data. The data then passes through the gateway and proxy server before reaching the cloud server for further processing and analytics. See Lecture 5: Basics of IoT Networking — Part-I @ 07:30

2.q: [Week 2] In MQTT, which field of a published message is used by the broker as routing information?
2.solution: The MQTT broker dispatches messages between senders and receivers. The topic included in a published message provides the routing information that the broker uses to deliver the message to clients subscribed to the matching topic. Answer Location: Week 2, Module 6 (Basics of IoT Networking - Part II) @ 08:27

2.q: [Week 2] Which of the following statements about MQTT topic wildcards are correct?
options: The plus sign (+) matches an arbitrary value at exactly one hierarchy level.
The hash sign (#) can be used to subscribe to all underlying hierarchy levels.
The subscription house/# matches only the exact topic house.
The subscription house/+/temperature can match house/kitchen/temperature.
2.solution: The plus sign (+) is a single-level wildcard, whereas the hash sign (#) is a multilevel wildcard. Thus, house/+/temperature can match house/kitchen/temperature, and house/# matches all topics whose hierarchy begins with house, not only the exact topic house. Answer Location: Week 2, Module 6 (Basics of IoT Networking - Part II) @ 12:01

2.q: [Week 2] Which of the following are main stages of Secure MQTT (SMQTT)?
2.solution: SMQTT consists of four main stages: setup, encryption, publish, and decryption. Route discovery is not one of the SMQTT stages. Answer Location: Week 2, Module 6 (Basics of IoT Networking - Part II) @ 13:45

2.q: [Week 2] At the transport layer, CoAP (Constrained Application Protocol) operates over which protocol?
2.solution: CoAP is designed for constrained environments and operates over UDP at the transport layer. Its lightweight design helps reduce communication overhead for resource-constrained IoT devices. Answer Location: Week 2, Module 7 (Basics of IoT Networking - Part III) @ 05:41

2.q: [Week 2] State True or False. In CoAP, a piggyback response is carried with the acknowledgment, whereas in the separate mode, the server response is sent in a message separate from the acknowledgment.
2.solution: In the piggyback mode, the server places its response in the acknowledgment message. In the separate mode, the acknowledgment is sent first and the response is transmitted later as a separate message. Answer Location: Week 2, Module 7 (Basics of IoT Networking - Part III) @ 07:48

2.q: [Week 2] Which of the following CoAP request-method mappings are correct?
2.solution: As presented in the lecture, CoAP uses GET, PUT, PUSH, and DELETE requests to retrieve, create, update, and delete data, respectively. Answer Location: Week 2, Module 7 (Basics of IoT Networking - Part III) @ 07:48

2.q: [Week 2] Which AMQP frame type is used to control the message-flow rate?
2.solution: The Flow frame controls the rate of message flow between AMQP peers. By comparison, Transfer carries messages, Disposition communicates a change in transfer state, and Detach terminates a link. Answer Location: Week 2, Module 8 (Basics of IoT Networking - Part IV) @ 06:21

2.q: [Week 2] Which of the following statements about AMQP components are correct?
options: An exchange receives messages and routes them to queues.
A queue stores messages for business processes or consumers.
A binding specifies message-distribution rules between an exchange and queues.
A consumer must route every producer message before it reaches an exchange.
2.solution: The main AMQP components discussed in the lecture are exchanges, queues, and bindings. An exchange receives and routes messages, a queue stores messages for consumers or business processes, and a binding defines the distribution rules connecting exchanges to queues. Answer Location: Week 2, Module 8 (Basics of IoT Networking - Part IV) @ 08:03

2.q: [Week 2] Which of the following IEEE 802.15.4 variant-application pairs are correct?
2.solution: The lecture associates IEEE 802.15.4c with China, 802.15.4d with Japan, 802.15.4e with industrial applications, 802.15.4f with active RFID, and 802.15.4g with smart utility networks. Answer Location: Week 2, Module 9 (Connectivity Technologies - Part I) @ 09:03

2.q: [Week 2] In a non-beacon-enabled IEEE 802.15.4 network, data frames are transmitted using:
2.solution: Non-beacon-enabled IEEE 802.15.4 networks transmit data frames using unslotted CSMA/CA. In contrast, beacon-enabled networks use slotted CSMA/CA with a superframe structure managed by the PAN coordinator. Answer Location: Week 2, Module 9 (Connectivity Technologies - Part I) @ 14:11

2.q: [Week 2] Which statement correctly describes the relationship between IEEE 802.15.4 and ZigBee?
options: IEEE 802.15.4 provides layers 1 and 2, while ZigBee extends the functionality to layer 3 and above.
ZigBee provides only the physical layer, while IEEE 802.15.4 provides all higher layers.
Both standards operate only at the application layer.
ZigBee and IEEE 802.15.4 are identical standards with no functional distinction.
2.solution: IEEE 802.15.4 primarily specifies the physical and MAC layers. ZigBee operates on top of these layers and adds higher-layer functions, including authentication, encryption, routing, forwarding, and support for mesh networking. Answer Location: Week 2, Module 9 (Connectivity Technologies - Part I) @ 16:08

2.q: [Week 2] Which of the following statements characterizes a ZigBee end device?
options: It communicates with its parent node.
It cannot relay data for other devices.
It forms the network root and acts as the trust center.
2.solution: A ZigBee end device has sufficient functionality to communicate with its parent, but it cannot relay data for other devices. It is therefore a reduced-functionality device. The coordinator, not an end device, forms the network root and may act as the trust center. Answer Location: Week 2, Module 9 (Connectivity Technologies - Part I) @ 23:54

2.q: [Week 2] Which option correctly describes addressing in 6LoWPAN?
options: A 16-bit address is globally unique, while a 64-bit address is PAN-specific.
A 16-bit short address is PAN-specific and assigned by the PAN coordinator, while a 64-bit extended address is globally unique.
Both 16-bit and 64-bit addresses are globally unique and assigned by an Internet router.
Both address types are used only for multicast communication.
2.solution: 6LoWPAN supports 16-bit short addresses for PAN-specific communication; these are assigned by the PAN coordinator. It also supports 64-bit extended addresses, which are globally unique. Answer Location: Week 2, Module 10 (Connectivity Technologies - Part II) @ 04:58

2.q: [Week 2] State True or False. In LOADng routing, an intermediate router may respond to a Route Request (RREQ) whenever it already has an active route to the requested destination.
2.solution: In LOADng, only the destination is permitted to respond to an RREQ. Intermediate LOADng routers are explicitly prohibited from responding, even when they have an active route to the requested destination. Answer Location: Week 2, Module 10 (Connectivity Technologies - Part II) @ 12:48

2.q: [Week 2] How does a passive RFID tag obtain the power required to transmit information?
options: It uses its own internal battery.
It is powered inductively by an RFID reader.
It receives power through a wired AIDC connection.
It does not require any source of power.
2.solution: Passive RFID tags do not have their own power supply. They must first be powered inductively by an RFID reader before they can transmit information. Active RFID tags, in contrast, have their own power supply. Answer Location: Week 2, Module 10 (Connectivity Technologies - Part II) @ 19:30

3.q: [Week 3] State whether the following statement is true or false. Statement: There is no network layer in Wired HART
3.solution: There is no network layer in Wired HART. See lecture 11 @ 05:22

3.q: [Week 3] Zwave operates at ________ MHz in the US and ________ MHz in Europe.
3.solution: Zwave operates at 908.42 MHz in the US and 868.42 MHz in Europe. See lecture 13 @ 3:40

3.q: [Week 3] Dumb behavior of sensor nodes is _______________ in nature (as it is dependent on the effects of the environmental conditions).
3.solution: Dumb behavior of sensor nodes is Temporal in nature (as it is dependent on the effects of the environmental conditions). See lecture 15 @ 05:40

3.q: [Week 3] The process of identifying channels consistently affected by interference and removing them from use is known as _________________.
3.solution: Channel Blacklisting identifies channels consistently affected by interference and removes them from use. See lecture 11 @ 07:30

3.q: [Week 3] The full form of NFC is
3.solution: The full form of NFC is Near Field Communication. See lecture 11 @ 17:44

3.q: [Week 3] State true or false. NFC works on the principle of magnetic induction.
3.solution: NFC works on the principle of magnetic induction. See lecture 11 @ 21:00

3.q: [Week 3] State whether the following statement is true or false. Statement: NFC tags found in supermarket products are examples of active NFC.
3.solution: Passive NFC tags found in supermarket products are examples of passive NFC. See lecture 11 @ 18:47
Bluetooth is based on Piconets. See lecture 12 @ 01:55

3.q: [Week 3] A __________ in NFC emits a small electric current which creates a magnetic field that in turn bridges the physical space between the devices.
3.solution: A reader in NFC emits a small electric current which creates a magnetic field that in turn bridges the physical space between the devices See lecture 11 @ 20:31

3.q: [Week 3] State true of false. Bluetooth technology is based on Ad-hoc network technology.
3.solution: Bluetooth technology is based on Ad-hoc network technology. See lecture 12 @ 02:30

3.q: [Week 3] State true or false. Zwave utilizes GFSK modulation and Hongkong channel encoding.
3.solution: Zwave utilizes GFSK modulation and Manchester channel encoding. See lecture 13 @ 07:36

3.q: [Week 3] The process of bypassing radio dead-spots is done using a message called ________ in Zwave.
3.solution: The process of bypassing radio dead-spots is done using a message called Healing in Zwave. See lecture 13 @ 11:34

3.q: [Week 3] State whether the following statement is true or false. Statement: Sensor nodes have unlimited battery life.
3.solution: Sensors nodes have limited battery life. See lecture 14 @ 13:15

3.q: [Week 3] State whether the following statement is true or false. Statement: The Link Manager Protocol in Bluetooth manages the establishment, authentication, link configuration.
3.solution: The Link Manager Protocol in Bluetooth manages the establishment, authentication, link configuration. See Page number – 157, Chapter - 7, Book - Introduction to IoT, Authors – Sudip Misra, Anandarup Mukherjee, and Arijit Roy, Publisher – Cambridge University Press, Edition – 1 (2021)

Zigbee commonly uses 250 kbps data rate. See Page number – 131, Chapter - 7, Book - Introduction to IoT, Authors – Sudip Misra, Anandarup Mukherjee, and Arijit Roy, Publisher – Cambridge University Press, Edition – 1 (2021)

4.q: [Week 4] What does the ultrasonic sensor measure generally in the AID system?
4.solution: In the Agricultural Intrusion Detection system, the ultrasonic sensor measures the distance at which the detected object is located. See Lecture 16: Sensor Networks – Part III @ 13:22

4.q: [Week 4] Which component processes the data received from the sensors in the AID system?
4.solution: The microcontroller processes the data received from the sensors in the AID system. See Lecture 16: Sensor Networks - Part III @ 17:07
The lecture discusses electromagnetic and molecular communication for nanodevices. See Lecture 16: Sensor Networks - Part III @ 25:11

4.q: [Week 4] When does sensing coverage guarantee network connectivity?
options: When the transmission range is at least twice the sensing range
When the sensing range is at least twice the transmission range
When the transmission and sensing ranges are equal
When the transmission range is smaller than the sensing range
4.solution: Sensing coverage guarantees connectivity when the transmission range is at least twice the sensing range. See Lecture 17: Sensor Networks - Part IV @ 04:14

4.q: [Week 4] Which of the following is a coverage problem in a static WSN?
4.solution: Area coverage is a standard coverage problem in a static wireless sensor network. The other options are networking tasks, not coverage categories. See Lecture 17: Sensor Networks - Part IV @ 11:30

4.q: [Week 4] Which reporting method is used for forest-fire monitoring in a WSN?
4.solution: Forest-fire monitoring uses event-driven reporting because sensor nodes report data when a fire-related event is detected. The lecture contrasts this with on-demand reporting, such as an inventory- control system. See Lecture 17: Sensor Networks – Part IV @ 01:44.

4.q: [Week 4] What does a data mule do?
options: Collects data and carries it to the sink
4.solution: A data mule visits sensor nodes, collects their data, and delivers it to the sink. See Lecture 18: Sensor Networks - Part V @ 07:15

4.q: [Week 4] What may happen if a critical stationary sensor node fails?
options: The network repairs itself by movement
4.solution: Failure of a critical stationary node may divide the network into disconnected parts. See Lecture 18: Sensor Networks - Part V @ 00:43

4.q: [Week 4] A person who provides sensing information acts as a:
4.solution: In human-centric sensing, a person may act as a data source by providing or collecting information. See Lecture 18: Sensor Networks - Part V @ 12:35

4.q: [Week 4] Which is an advantage of a stationary wireless sensor network?
4.solution: In a stationary wireless sensor network, sensor nodes remain fixed. Therefore, deployment and topology maintenance are comparatively easier. See Lecture 18: Sensor Networks – Part V @ 00:43

4.q: [Week 4] State whether the following statement is True or False. Statement: In a UAV network, the network topology may change frequently because the UAVs are mobile.
4.solution: UAVs move from one location to another, causing frequent changes in their relative positions and communication links. Therefore, the network topology may change frequently. See Lecture 19: UAV Networks @ 05:23

4.q: [Week 4] Which is a common issue in UAV networks?
4.solution: UAV movement causes frequent changes in network topology and communication links. See Lecture 19: UAV Networks @ 05:23

4.q: [Week 4] Compared with traditional SCADA, M2M supports:
4.solution: Traditional SCADA commonly uses isolated proprietary systems, while M2M supports cross-platform integration. See Lecture 20: Machine to Machine Communication @ 04:28

4.q: [Week 4] State whether the following statement is True or False. Statement: In a stationary wireless sensor network, sensor nodes can automatically move to restore connectivity after a node failure.
4.solution: In a stationary wireless sensor network, sensor nodes remain fixed. Therefore, they cannot move automatically to repair connectivity after a node failure. See Lecture 18: Sensor Networks – Part V @ 00:43

4.q: [Week 4] Which statement best describes M2M communication?
options: Devices can exchange data without direct human control
Every data exchange must be performed manually
Only one device can communicate at a time
Devices cannot communicate through a network
4.solution: M2M communication allows machines or devices to exchange data automatically. Human intervention may still be required for maintenance and operational stability. See Lecture 20: Machine to Machine Communication @ 09:24.

5.q: [Week 5] What does interoperability allow IoT devices to do?
5.solution: Interoperability enables different IoT devices and systems to communicate and exchange data. See Lecture 21 (Interoperability in Internet of Things) @ 03:30
Syntactic interoperability concerns the format of messages exchanged between devices and users. See Lecture 21 (Interoperability in Internet of Things) @ 17:01
UMB stands for Universal Middleware Bridge. It helps different middleware-based devices work together. See Lecture 21 (Interoperability in Internet of Things) @ 25:42

5.q: [Week 5] What is the operating voltage of the Arduino UNO?
5.solution: The Arduino UNO operates at 5 volts. See Lecture 22: Introduction to Arduino Programming – Part I @ 06:57.

5.q: [Week 5] What is a program written in the Arduino IDE called?
5.solution: A program created and uploaded using the Arduino IDE is called a sketch. See Lecture 22 (Introduction to Arduino Programming - Part I) @ 12:12

5.q: [Week 5] Which interface is mainly used to connect an Arduino UNO to a computer?
5.solution: The Arduino UNO uses a USB interface to connect to a computer. The USB connection can be used to upload programs to the board and also provide power during development. See Lecture 22: Introduction to Arduino Programming – Part I @ 07:26

5.q: [Week 5] What is the conventional starting index of an array in Arduino programming?
5.solution: As in C and C++, Arduino arrays use zero-based indexing. Therefore, the first element is stored at index 0. See Lecture 23 (Introduction to Arduino Programming - Part II) @ 04:08

5.q: [Week 5] Which Arduino function is used to generate a pseudo-random number within a specified range?
5.solution: The random() function generates a pseudo-random number in a specified range. For example, random(max) produces a value within the range defined by max. See Lecture 23 (Introduction to Arduino Programming - Part II) @ 09:19

5.q: [Week 5] In the traffic-control example, which LED is switched ON first to represent the GO signal?
5.solution: The traffic() function first sets the green LED HIGH and displays the GO message. After a delay, it switches to yellow and then red. See Lecture 23 (Introduction to Arduino Programming - Part II) @ 14:34

5.q: [Week 5] Which quantities are measured by a DHT sensor?
5.solution: A DHT sensor measures the temperature and humidity of its surroundings. See Lecture 24: Integration of Sensors and Actuators with Arduino – Part I @ 04:37.

5.q: [Week 5] What does a sensor convert a physical quantity into?
5.solution: A sensor is an electronic element that converts a physical quantity or measurement into an electrical signal. See Lecture 24: Integration of Sensors and Actuators with Arduino – Part I, Sensors section.

5.q: [Week 5] In the DHT sensor sketch, delay(2000) causes successive readings to be printed after approximately how much time?
5.solution: The delay() function takes time in milliseconds. Therefore, delay(2000) introduces a delay of 2000 milliseconds, which equals 2 seconds. See Lecture 24 (Integration of Sensors and Actuators with Arduino - Part I) @ 13:34

5.q: [Week 5] State whether the following statement is True or False. Statement: A servo motor is a low-precision motor used only for linear motion.
5.solution: A servo motor is a high-precision motor that provides controlled rotary motion. See Lecture 25: Integration of Sensors and Actuators with Arduino – Part II @ 04:30.

5.q: [Week 5] Which device provides controlled rotary motion?
5.solution: A servo motor is an actuator that provides precise and controlled rotary motion. See Lecture 25: Integration of Sensors and Actuators with Arduino – Part II @ 04:30.

5.q: [Week 5] State whether the following statement is True or False. Statement: A stepper motor is a type of actuator.
5.solution: A stepper motor is one of the motor actuators discussed in the lecture. Other examples include servo motors, hydraulic motors, solenoids, relays, and AC motors. See Lecture 25: Integration of Sensors and Actuators with Arduino – Part II @ 03:20.

6.q: [Week 6] What are the five basic data types available in Python, as introduced in the lecture?
6.solution: The lecture states that Python has five data types: Numbers, String, List, Tuple, and Dictionary. See Lecture 26 (Introduction to Python Programming – Part I) @ 15:50

6.q: [Week 6] Which keyword is used to define a function in Python?
6.solution: A function in Python is defined using the def keyword, followed by the function name and its arguments. See Lecture 26 (Introduction to Python Programming – Part I) @ 19:20

6.q: [Week 6] In Python's exception handling, which keyword is used to handle an exception raised inside the try block?
6.solution: Python uses the try, except and else block structure for exception handling; the except block catches the exception raised in the try block. See Lecture 26 (Introduction to Python Programming – Part I) @ 28:55

6.q: [Week 6] Which mode of Python's open() function is used to add data to the end of an existing file without erasing its existing content?
6.solution: Python supports four basic file modes: r (read), w (write), a (append), and r+ (read and write). The append mode adds new data to the end of the file without deleting existing content. See Lecture 27 (Introduction to Python Programming – Part II) @ 02:55

6.q: [Week 6] Which Python library, installable via pip, is used for image read/write operations as covered in the lecture?
6.solution: PIL (Python Image Library) is used to work with image files. It is installed using 'sudo pip install pillow'; PIL supports up to Python 2.7 while Pillow supports Python 3.x. See Lecture 27 (Introduction to Python Programming – Part II) @ 17:25

6.q: [Week 6] Which socket_type value is used while creating a TCP/IP socket in Python's socket module?
6.solution: A socket is created using socket.socket(socket_family, socket_type, protocol). For a TCP/IP (connection-oriented) socket, socket_family is AF_INET and socket_type is SOCK_STREAM. See Lecture 27 (Introduction to Python Programming – Part II) @ 24:40

6.q: [Week 6] How many GPIO pins does the Raspberry Pi 3 Model B have, as shown in the specifications table?
6.solution: As per the specifications table, the Raspberry Pi 3 Model B, Raspberry Pi 2 Model B, and Raspberry Pi Zero all have 40 GPIO pins. See Lecture 28 (Introduction to Raspberry Pi – Part I) @ 05:10

6.q: [Week 6] Which of the following is an officially supported operating system for Raspberry Pi mentioned in the lecture?
6.solution: Raspbian and NOOBS are the officially supported operating systems for Raspberry Pi. Ubuntu Mate, Snappy Ubuntu Core, Windows 10 Core, Pinet, and RISC OS are examples of third-party operating systems. See Lecture 28 (Introduction to Raspberry Pi – Part I) @ 12:05

6.q: [Week 6] Raspberry Pi is best described as a:
6.solution: The lecture introduces Raspberry Pi as a computer that fits in your palm — a low-cost, single-board computer that is easy to access and use. See Lecture 28 (Introduction to Raspberry Pi – Part I) @ 04:45

6.q: [Week 6] Which command is used to install the GPIO library on Raspberry Pi before programming the blinking LED example?
6.solution: After installing Python development tools using 'sudo apt-get install python-dev', the GPIO library is installed using 'sudo apt-get install python-rpi.gpio'. See Lecture 29 (Introduction to Raspberry Pi – Part II) @ 07:43

6.q: [Week 6] Where is the CSI camera connector slot located on the Raspberry Pi board?
options: Between the Ethernet port and the HDMI port
Next to the power supply pin
On the underside of the board
6.solution: The Raspberry Pi Camera connects through a dedicated CSI slot, which is placed between the Ethernet port and the HDMI port on the board. See Lecture 29 (Introduction to Raspberry Pi – Part II) @ 18:27

6.q: [Week 6] Which terminal command captures a still image using the Raspberry Pi camera?
6.solution: Running 'raspistill -o image.jpg' in the terminal captures an image using the Raspberry Pi camera and stores it as image.jpg. See Lecture 29 (Introduction to Raspberry Pi – Part II) @ 19:35

6.q: [Week 6] What does DHT stand for in the DHT sensor used with Raspberry Pi in the auto-cooling system?
6.solution: DHT stands for Digital Humidity and Temperature Sensor. It has 4 pins: PIN 1 (3.3V–5V power supply), PIN 2 (Data), PIN 3 (Null), and PIN 4 (Ground). See Lecture 30 (Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi – Part I) @ 05:20

6.q: [Week 6] How many output terminals does the relay used in the temperature-dependent auto-cooling system have, as shown in the lecture?
6.solution: The relay is a mechanical/electromechanical switch with 3 output terminals (left to right): NO (normal open), Common, and NC (normal close). See Lecture 30 (Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi – Part I) @ 07:50

6.q: [Week 6] State whether the following statement is True or False. Statement: In the temperature-dependent auto-cooling system, the fan operates when the surrounding temperature rises above the threshold value specified in the code.
6.solution: The lecture demonstrates that the fan is switched on whenever the measured temperature exceeds the threshold value set in the program. See Lecture 30 (Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi – Part I) @ 18:14

7.q: [Week 7] In the remote data logging system, which socket type is used to send sensor data from the client to the server?
7.solution: The client creates a UDP socket using socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM) to send the sensor readings to the server. See Lecture 31 (Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi – Part 2) @ 07:10

7.q: [Week 7] Which Adafruit function is used in the client code to read humidity and temperature values from the DHT sensor?
7.solution: The sensordata() function calls Adafruit_DHT.read_retry(sensor,17), which returns the humidity and temperature values from the DHT sensor. See Lecture 31 (Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi – Part 2) @ 04:50

7.q: [Week 7] Where does the server in the remote data logging example save the data received from the client as mentioned in the lecture?
options: In a text file named Datalog.txt
7.solution: The server code opens 'Datalog.txt' in append mode and writes the received message from the client into this text file. See Lecture 31 (Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi – Part 2) @ 15:40

7.q: [Week 7] Which Python string function is used to split the comma-separated sensor data into separate values on the server?
7.solution: The split() function splits a string into multiple strings based on a specified separator/delimiter, e.g. Data.split(",") splits data wherever a comma is found. See Lecture 32 (Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi – Part 3) @ 08:40

7.q: [Week 7] State whether the following statement is True or False. Statement: Matplotlib Python library is used to plot the temperature and humidity data received at the server in the lecture.
7.solution: MATPLOTLIB is a Python library used to create 2D plots; functions such as plot(), xlabel(), ylabel(), and title() are used to plot and label the sensor data. See Lecture 32 (Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi – Part 3) @ 12:15

7.q: [Week 7] Which matplotlib function turns on interactive mode so that the plot updates in real time as new data arrives?
7.solution: ion() turns on the interactive mode in matplotlib. Other common plotting functions mentioned include figure(), grid(), subplot(), close(), and scatter(). See Lecture 32 (Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi – Part 3) @ 23:25

7.q: [Week 7] In a traditional (non-SDN) network, where does the routing protocol logic (e.g., OSPF) mainly execute?
7.solution: In the current network, protocols like OSPF execute at the switches, which forward traffic in a distributed manner with no centralized control. See Lecture 33 (Software-Defined Networking – Part I) @ 04:10

7.q: [Week 7] In which year was the OpenFlow project — from which the idea of software-defined networking originated — presented at ACM SIGCOMM?
7.solution: The idea of software-defined networking originated from the OpenFlow project, presented at ACM SIGCOMM in 2008. Stanford published the OpenFlow V1.0.0 specification the following year. See Lecture 33 (Software-Defined Networking – Part I) @ 10:50

7.q: [Week 7] What message does a switch send to the SDN controller when it receives a packet for which no matching flow-rule exists?
7.solution: When no flow-rule is present for an incoming request, the switch sends a PACKET-IN message to the controller, which then decides a suitable flow-rule and inserts it at the switch. See Lecture 33 (Software-Defined Networking – Part I) @ 22:33

7.q: [Week 7] Which SDN API is used for communication between the control layer and the infrastructure layer?
7.solution: The Southbound API is used to communicate between the control layer and the infrastructure layer using the OpenFlow protocol. The Northbound API communicates between the control and application layers. See Lecture 34 (Software-Defined Networking – Part II) @ 02:00

7.q: [Week 7] According to the lecture, approximately how many requests per second can a typical SDN controller handle through a single thread?
7.solution: The lecture states that a controller can typically handle around 200 requests in a second through a single thread. See Lecture 34 (Software-Defined Networking – Part II) @ 04:10

7.q: [Week 7] Which control mechanism is described where the entire network's control decisions are taken by a single controller?
7.solution: In centralized control, control decisions are taken in a centralized manner by a single controller, unlike distributed control where each subnetwork is controlled by a different controller. See Lecture 34 (Software-Defined Networking – Part II) @ 08:15

7.q: [Week 7] Which of the following is listed as a benefit of integrating SDN with IoT?
7.solution: Benefits of integrating SDN in IoT include intelligent routing decisions, simplified information collection/analysis/decision-making, visibility of network resources, and intelligent traffic pattern analysis. See Lecture 35 (Software-Defined IoT Networking – Part I) @ 02:50

7.q: [Week 7] According to the lecture, what is a key resource-constraint challenge in wireless sensor networks that motivates software-defined WSN?
7.solution: Wireless sensor network challenges include real-time programming of sensor nodes, vendor-specific architecture, resource-constrained devices, and limited memory, meaning too many control programs cannot be inserted. See Lecture 35 (Software-Defined IoT Networking – Part I) @ 08:10

7.q: [Week 7] In the SDN-WISE protocol stack for sensor nodes, what does "INPP" stand for?
7.solution: In the SDN-WISE protocol stack, the forwarding layer above IEEE 802.15.4 consists of flow-rules, and INPP stands for In Network Packet Processing. See Lecture 35 (Software-Defined IoT Networking – Part I) @ 15:35

8.q: [Week 8] Which of the following is listed as a problem in traditional (non-SDN) mobile networks?
options: Difficult to scale due to static, over-provisioned networks
8.solution: Traditional mobile networks are difficult to scale because static, over-provisioned networks are inflexible to manage high-demand mobile traffic; they are also difficult to manage, inflexible, and cost-expensive. See Lecture 36 (Software-Defined IoT Networking – Part II, slide 3)

8.q: [Week 8] In the ODIN architecture for software-defined wireless networks, what does the 'Odin agent' do?
options: It is placed at the controller end to manage policies
It replaces the OpenFlow protocol entirely
It is placed with the physical devices to communicate with the controller
It performs billing for cloud resources
8.solution: In ODIN, an agent is placed at access points (with the physical devices) to communicate with the controller, while the Odin master resides at the controller end. See Lecture 36 (Software-Defined IoT Networking – Part II, slide 11)

8.q: [Week 8] What is the primary goal of Mobi-Flow's proactive rule placement approach in Software-Defined IoT?
options: To place flow-rules randomly across all access points
To predict users' future location and place flow-rules at APs accordingly
To eliminate the need for a controller
To increase the number of PACKET-IN messages
8.solution: Mobi-Flow predicts the location of end-users at time (t+1) while they are at time (t), and places flow-rules at the access points that can be associated with the users based on their predicted locations, using an order-K Markov predictor. See Lecture 36 (Software-Defined IoT Networking – Part II, slides 15–16)

8.q: [Week 8] Which simulation tool is mentioned in the lecture for experimenting with wireless software-defined networks, supporting both wired and wireless (IEEE 802.11) protocols?
8.solution: Mininet-WiFi can be used to deploy a network supporting both wired (Ethernet) and wireless (WiFi, IEEE 802.11) protocols, while ONOS can be used to place the controllers. See Lecture 36 (Software-Defined IoT Networking – Part II, slide 21)

8.q: [Week 8] According to the NIST definition quoted in the lecture, cloud computing enables on-demand network access to a shared pool of what?
8.solution: NIST defines cloud computing as a model for enabling convenient, on-demand network access to a shared pool of configurable computing resources such as networks, servers, storage, and applications. See Lecture 37 (Cloud Computing – Fundamentals, slide 4)

8.q: [Week 8] Which of the following is one of the essential characteristics of cloud computing as defined by NIST?
8.solution: NIST lists rapid elasticity as an essential characteristic, meaning cloud resource allocation and release should be rapid, elastic, and automatic, giving consumers the impression of infinite resources. See Lecture 37 (Cloud Computing – Fundamentals, slide 9)

8.q: [Week 8] Which cloud deployment model is set up for the exclusive use of a single organization, typically managed on-premises or by a third party off-premises?
8.solution: A private cloud is a cloud set-up functioned only for a single organization, typically managed by the organization itself (on-premises) or by a third party (off-premises). See Lecture 37 (Cloud Computing – Fundamentals, slide 20)

8.q: [Week 8] Which of the following is given as an example of a public cloud provider in the lecture?
options: A company's internal private data center
A single organization's dedicated server room
A community-only cloud shared by hospitals
8.solution: Public cloud examples given include Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Compute Engine, and Microsoft Azure — cloud set-ups available for the use of any person or industry. See Lecture 37 (Cloud Computing – Fundamentals, slide 19)

8.q: [Week 8] Which cloud service model provides on-demand delivery of computing infrastructure such as servers, storage, network, and operating system?
8.solution: Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) contains the basic building blocks for cloud IT, providing access to networking features, computers (virtual or dedicated hardware), storage, and operating systems. See Lecture 38 (Cloud Computing – Service Models, slide 4)

8.q: [Week 8] In the IaaS working methodology, which component allows multiple virtual machines to share the same physical hardware?
8.solution: In IaaS, the hypervisor sits above the physical hardware and manages multiple virtual machines (VMs), each running its own operating system, on a virtualized server. See Lecture 38 (Cloud Computing – Service Models, slide 5)

8.q: [Week 8] Which cloud service model is described as 'application middleware offered as a service to developers', removing the need to manage underlying hardware and operating systems?
8.solution: Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) removes the need for organizations to manage underlying infrastructure (hardware and OS) and lets developers focus on deploying and managing their applications; it is described as application middleware offered as a service. See Lecture 38 (Cloud Computing – Service Models, slide 15)

8.q: [Week 8] What is the primary purpose of a Service Level Agreement (SLA) in cloud service management?
options: To define the physical location of the data center
To define the non-functional requirements expected from the service provider
To specify the programming language used by the cloud provider
To list the hardware vendors used by the provider
8.solution: An SLA defines the non-functional requirements expected from the service provider and provides a roadmap with clearly defined deliverables, describing the quality, utility, and warranty of services expected by the customer. See Lecture 39 (Cloud Computing – Service Management and Security, slide 4)

8.q: [Week 8] In cloud service accounting and billing, what does 'service accounting' primarily aim to obtain?
options: Resource usage information, typically in the form of records
The source code of hosted applications
The marketing budget of the provider
8.solution: Service accounting aims to obtain resource usage information, typically in the form of records, depending on infrastructure and service monitoring where usage information is obtained from metric measurements. See Lecture 39 (Cloud Computing – Service Management and Security, slide 5)

8.q: [Week 8] What is the main purpose of using cloud simulators such as CloudSim before actual deployment?
options: To permanently replace the need for real cloud infrastructure
To increase the billing cost of cloud services
To provide a reliable, scalable, and repeatable environment for pre-deployment performance evaluation
8.solution: Simulation tools provide a reliable, scalable, and repeatable environment for performance evaluation, facilitating pre-deployment tests of services at no cost and enabling repeatable evaluation. See Lecture 40 (Cloud Computing – Case Studies, slides 2–3)

8.q: [Week 8] CloudSim, a widely used cloud simulation framework, was developed at which institution and is based on which programming language?
options: CLOUDS Lab, University of Melbourne, based on Java
8.solution: CloudSim is a simulation framework that models cloud computing environments (data centers, VMs, applications, users, and network topology), written in a Java-based environment, and developed at the CLOUDS Lab of the University of Melbourne. See Lecture 40 (Cloud Computing – Case Studies, slide 5)

9.q: [Week 9] OpenStack was launched in 2010 as a joint project between Rackspace Hosting and which other organization?
9.solution: OpenStack, a software used to create cloud infrastructure, was launched as a joint project of Rackspace Hosting and NASA in 2010, and is open source. See Lecture 41 (Cloud Computing – Practical, slide 3)

9.q: [Week 9] Which OpenStack component provides the dashboard (GUI) that gives an overview of the other components?
9.solution: Horizon is the dashboard component of OpenStack — it provides the GUI of the software and gives an overview of the other components. See Lecture 41 (Cloud Computing – Practical, slide 5)

9.q: [Week 9] Which OpenStack component is the compute service where instances are launched?
9.solution: Nova is the compute service in OpenStack — it is where you launch your instances. Glance is the image service, Cinder is block storage, and Neutron provides networking. See Lecture 41 (Cloud Computing – Practical, slide 5)

9.q: [Week 9] Which script/tool is used in the lecture to install OpenStack, requiring the local.conf file to be configured with passwords and host IP before running?
9.solution: OpenStack is installed using Devstack: after cloning the devstack repository and configuring local.conf with ADMIN_PASSWORD, DATABASE_PASSWORD, RABBIT_PASSWORD, SERVICE_PASSWORD, and HOST_IP, the stack.sh file is run to install it. See Lecture 41 (Cloud Computing – Practical, slides 9–10)

9.q: [Week 9] According to the lecture, what does sensor-cloud fundamentally provide, beyond merely integrating sensors with cloud computing?
options: A physical replacement for all sensor hardware
Virtualization of sensor nodes, offered on a pay-per-use basis
A way to eliminate the need for a sink node
9.solution: Sensor-cloud is not mere integration of sensors and cloud computing or 'dumping sensor data into the cloud' — it introduces the concept of virtualization of the sensor node, offered on a pay-per-use basis, acting as a stratum between sensor nodes and end-users. See Lecture 42 (Sensor-Cloud – Part I: Sensor-as-a-Service, slide 10)

9.q: [Week 9] In a traditional Wireless Sensor Network (WSN), who is typically responsible for redeployment of the sensor nodes?
9.solution: In a traditional WSN, the WSN-user is responsible for ownership, deployment, redeployment, maintenance, overhead, and usage. In sensor-cloud, redeployment and maintenance shift to the Sensor-Cloud Service Provider (SCSP), while usage shifts to the end-user. See Lecture 42 (Sensor-Cloud – Part I: Sensor-as-a-Service, slide 12)

9.q: [Week 9] In the sensor-cloud model, which actor purchases physical sensor devices and lends them to the sensor-cloud, playing a role from a business perspective?
9.solution: The Sensor-owner purchases physical sensor devices deployed over different geographical locations and lends these devices to the sensor-cloud, acting as a business actor. See Lecture 42 (Sensor-Cloud – Part I: Sensor-as-a-Service, slide 13)

9.q: [Week 9] Which of the following is listed as a major limitation of traditional WSNs that motivates the sensor-cloud model?
options: Difficulty adapting to a change of requirement (e.g., moving from agriculture to smart home use)
9.solution: Limitations of WSNs include procurement issues (price, right vendor, sensor types), deployment and maintenance overheads, and difficulty adapting to a change of requirement — e.g., a WSN built for agriculture cannot easily be repurposed for a smart home. See Lecture 42 (Sensor-Cloud – Part I: Sensor-as-a-Service, slide 9)

9.q: [Week 9] In the Optimal Composition of Virtual Sensors, what does CoV-I refer to?
options: Composition of virtual sensors spanning multiple geographic regions
Composition of virtual sensors using only homogeneous nodes within the same geographic region
A caching mechanism for sensor data
9.solution: CoV-I refers to the formation of a Virtual Sensor (VS) using homogeneous sensor nodes within the same geographical boundary, while CoV-II spans multiple regions using heterogeneous nodes to form a Virtual Sensor Group (VSG). See Lecture 43 (Sensor-Cloud – Part II: Sensor-as-a-Service, slide 6)

9.q: [Week 9] In the sensor-cloud caching mechanism, which cache handles requests directly from the end-user and decides whether to serve data directly or re-cache from another source?
9.solution: The Internal Cache (IC) handles requests from the end-user and takes the decision on whether the data should be provided directly or whether it is required to re-cache the data from the External Cache (EC). See Lecture 43 (Sensor-Cloud – Part II: Sensor-as-a-Service, slide 13)

9.q: [Week 9] Why is dynamic and adaptive data caching useful in sensor-cloud, according to the lecture?
options: Because environmental conditions always change extremely fast
Because it removes the need for a sensor-owner
Because caching eliminates the need for virtualization
Because unnecessary sensing during slow environmental change wastes energy
9.solution: In many cases, environmental conditions change quite slowly, so the sensed data of physical sensors remains largely unaltered; unnecessary sensing under such conditions causes needless energy consumption, motivating adaptive caching. See Lecture 43 (Sensor-Cloud – Part II: Sensor-as-a-Service, slide 12)

9.q: [Week 9] Which company is credited with coining the term 'fog computing'?
9.solution: Fog computing, or 'fogging,' is a term coined by CISCO. The idea is to extend the cloud nearer to IoT devices by introducing an intermediate layer between the cloud and the devices. See Lecture 44 (Fog Computing – Part I, slide 2)

9.q: [Week 9] Which of the following is listed as a key issue with the traditional cloud model that motivates fog computing?
options: Volume, latency, and bandwidth limitations of the cloud
Too much local processing power at the device level
9.solution: The current cloud model faces issues of Volume (too much data to process/store), Latency (round-trip time is too slow for time-sensitive data), and Bandwidth (huge traffic generated by billions of devices consumes most available bandwidth). See Lecture 44 (Fog Computing – Part I, slide 6)

9.q: [Week 9] Where is the fog layer positioned in the fog computing architecture?
options: Between the cloud and the IoT devices
There is no fixed position; it replaces the cloud entirely
9.solution: Fog is a layer between the cloud and IoT devices; many fog nodes can be present, and sensor data are processed in the fog before being sent to the cloud, reducing latency and saving bandwidth and cloud storage. See Lecture 45 (Fog Computing – Part II, slide 2)

9.q: [Week 9] Which of the following is NOT listed as a required characteristic of a fog node?
9.solution: Fog nodes need transient storage, computing facility (to process data and take quick decisions), and network connectivity to connect with IoT devices, other fog nodes, and the cloud — not permanent unlimited archival storage, which is the cloud's role. See Lecture 45 (Fog Computing – Part II, slide 4)

10.q: [Week 10] In the analogy comparing humans to smart cities presented in the lecture, what do 'Sensors and Tags' correspond to?
10.solution: In the human–smart city analogy, Sensors and Tags correspond to Sensory Organs, Buildings/Industries/People correspond to the Skeleton, digital telecommunication networks correspond to Nerves, and ubiquitously embedded intelligence corresponds to the Brain. See Lecture 46 (Smart Cities and Smart Homes – Part I, slide 3)

10.q: [Week 10] Which of the following is listed as one of the six 'Application Focus Areas' of a smart city?
10.solution: The six application focus areas listed are Smart Economy, Smart Governance, Smart People, Smart Mobility, Smart Environment, and Smart Living. See Lecture 46 (Smart Cities and Smart Homes – Part I, slide 4)

10.q: [Week 10] Under 'Current Focus Areas' of smart cities, which application area specifically deals with the auto routing of vehicles to empty slots and detecting vacant slots?
10.solution: Smart Parking Lots focus on auto routing of vehicles to empty slots, auto charging for services provided, and detection of vacant slots in the parking lot. See Lecture 46 (Smart Cities and Smart Homes – Part I, slide 11)

10.q: [Week 10] Which IoT challenge in smart cities relates to the risk of data leakage arising from multiple tenants sharing the same infrastructure?
10.solution: Under Security and Privacy challenges, the lecture notes exposure to attacks and vulnerabilities, and that multi-tenancy induces the risk of data leakage. See Lecture 46 (Smart Cities and Smart Homes – Part I, slide 16)

10.q: [Week 10] What is the primary purpose of data fusion in IoT-enabled smart city environments, as described in the lecture?
options: To delete redundant sensors from the network
To make the large incoming data volume precise and accurate for better decision making
To replace the need for any sensors
10.solution: Data fusion addresses the challenge of making large, incoming data volumes precise and accurate, since the quality of data precision and accuracy directly affects the quality of decision-making in IoT-enabled smart cities. See Lecture 47 (Smart Cities and Smart Homes – Part II, slide 2)

10.q: [Week 10] Which data fusion challenge refers to the situation where the same type of sensor reports different data for the same location?
10.solution: Conflicts arise when the same sensor type reports different data for the same location. Imperfection refers to inaccurate/uncertain sensor data, Ambiguity refers to outliers/missing data, and Alignment relates to converting sensor data frames to a singular frame. See Lecture 47 (Smart Cities and Smart Homes – Part II, slide 4)

10.q: [Week 10] In the stages of data fusion, at which level does the fusion of information happen at the sensor node or within the local network itself?
10.solution: Signal level fusion occurs at the sensor node or within the local network itself, while pixel level occurs at the imaging device, feature level occurs prior to decision making, and decision level is an ensemble of decisions. See Lecture 47 (Smart Cities and Smart Homes – Part II, slide 6)

10.q: [Week 10] Which of the following is listed as one of the three functional layers of a smart parking system?
10.solution: Smart parking has three functional layers: Information Collection, System Deployment, and Service Dissemination. See Lecture 47 (Smart Cities and Smart Homes – Part II, slide 11)

10.q: [Week 10] In the classification of energy harvesting solutions for smart cities, which type involves energy sources intentionally deployed near IoT devices?
10.solution: Dedicated energy harvesting involves energy sources intentionally deployed near IoT sources, with the amount of energy harvested depending on the sensitivity of the harvesting circuit, the distance between device and source, and the environment. See Lecture 48 (Smart Cities and Smart Homes – Part III, slide 18)

10.q: [Week 10] Which Home Area Network (HAN) standard is defined by IEEE 802.15.4 at the physical and MAC layers, and aims at low-cost, low-energy devices?
10.solution: Zigbee consists of four layers (Physical, MAC, Network, Application); the Physical and MAC layers are defined by IEEE 802.15.4, while Network and Application layers are defined by Zigbee itself, and it targets low-cost, low-energy devices. See Lecture 48 (Smart Cities and Smart Homes – Part III, slide 14)

10.q: [Week 10] Which HAN standard enables remote control of compliant devices over existing power lines and electrical wiring in a house, and is mainly used for lighting and appliance control?
10.solution: X-10 enables remote control of compliant transmitters and receivers over power lines and electrical wiring, is adopted by GE and Philips, has low speed and low data rate, and is mainly used for control of lighting, appliance networks, and security sensors. See Lecture 48 (Smart Cities and Smart Homes – Part III, slide 15)

10.q: [Week 10] According to the lecture, why does traditional TCP/IP fail to work well for Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication?
options: TCP/IP was designed mainly for single-pair information exchange dependent on data location
TCP/IP cannot be used with any wireless devices
TCP/IP requires no IP addresses at all
TCP/IP works only in stationary networks with no scalability limits
10.solution: TCP/IP is designed mainly for handling information exchange between a single pair of entities, is dependent on the location of data, and can only identify endpoint addresses — which alone is not useful for content distribution in highly mobile V2X environments. See Lecture 49 (Connected Vehicles – Part I, slide 7)

10.q: [Week 10] Which frequency spectrum did the US Department of Transport and FCC allocate for Intelligent Connected Vehicles (ICVs)?
10.solution: The US Department of Transport and Federal Communications Commission allocated 75 MHz (5850–5925 MHz) as the dedicated spectrum for ICVs, based on Dedicated Short Range Communication (DSRC) technology. See Lecture 50 (Connected Vehicles – Part II, slide 3)

10.q: [Week 10] In the phases of ICV development described in the lecture, which phase is based on 4G LTE or DSRC and focuses on intelligent transportation services?
10.solution: Phase-1 covers infotainment services based on 2G/3G, Phase-2 covers intelligent transportation services based on 4G LTE or DSRC, and Phase-3 covers vehicles connected to the cloud. See Lecture 50 (Connected Vehicles – Part II, slide 6)

10.q: [Week 10] In the VANET domain classification, which domain consists of vehicles (mobile) and Road-Side Units (RSUs, static), communicating via V2V or V2I using the DSRC stack?
10.solution: The Ad-hoc Domain is composed of vehicles (OBUs, which are mobile) and Road-Side Units (RSUs, which are static); communication may be V2V or V2I, carried out through the DSRC stack (IEEE 802.11p). See Lecture 50 (Connected Vehicles – Part II, slide 12)

11.q: [Week 11] According to the lecture, which feature distinguishes a smart grid from a traditional electrical grid?
options: Energy distribution is only one directional.
Monitoring and restoration are always performed manually.
It enables bidirectional flows of energy with two-way communication and control.
Energy generation must occur only at centralized power plants.
11.solution: The lecture describes a smart grid as a modernized grid that supports bidirectional energy flow and two-way communication and control, unlike the traditional grid's one-directional operation. See Lecture 51 (Smart Grid - Part I, slide 3)

11.q: [Week 11] What is the role of a smart meter in a smart home?
options: It generates electricity from renewable energy sources.
It provides the Smart Grid interface between the consumer and the energy service provider.
It replaces the home energy management system.
It operates only as a one-way energy meter without information exchange.
11.solution: Smart meters operate digitally and provide the interface for automated information exchange between the consumer side and the energy service provider. See Lecture 51 (Smart Grid - Part I, slide 14)

11.q: [Week 11] Under Time-of-Use pricing, when are consumers encouraged to operate smart appliances to reduce their energy cost?
options: Only when the grid has a blackout.
At a fixed time independent of the grid load.
11.solution: Time-of-Use pricing encourages consumers to shift energy consumption to off-peak periods, when grid load is lower and the price of energy is lower. See Lecture 51 (Smart Grid - Part I, slide 20)

11.q: [Week 11] In net metering, the consumer's final bill depends on which two energy flows?
options: Only the energy generated at centralized power plants.
Only the energy stored in the consumer's battery.
Energy inflow from the grid and energy outflow from the consumer to the grid.
11.solution: The lecture states that net-metering bills depend on both the energy received by the consumer from the grid and the excess energy supplied by the consumer back to the grid. See Lecture 51 (Smart Grid - Part I, slide 21)

11.q: [Week 11] Which device is used in a smart grid operation center to sample voltage and current for monitoring the transmission system?
11.solution: A PMU samples voltage and current at its installed location. Multiple PMUs form a phasor network whose information can be analyzed by a centralized SCADA system. See Lecture 52 (Smart Grid - Part II, slide 3)

11.q: [Week 11] Which of the following is a function of distribution intelligence in the smart grid?
options: Preventing all use of smart meters.
Identifying the source of a power outage and supporting automatic power-flow restoration.
Restricting the grid to one-way communication.
Removing protection and control from feeder lines.
11.solution: Distribution intelligence uses smart IoT devices and smart meters to identify outage sources, support automated switching, optimize real and reactive power, and protect feeder lines. See Lecture 52 (Smart Grid - Part II, slide 5)

11.q: [Week 11] In smart grid communication, what does a gateway connect?
options: Closely located smart meters to Data Aggregator Units (DAUs).
Only power plants directly to home appliances.
PMUs directly to plug-in electric vehicles.
Renewable generators directly to SCADA without intermediate communication.
11.solution: The lecture explains that a gateway connects a group of closely located smart meters and acts as the communication link between those smart meters and the DAUs. See Lecture 52 (Smart Grid - Part II, slide 11)

11.q: [Week 11] Which type of attack compromises the availability of smart grid components or information by making them inaccessible when needed?
11.solution: The lecture identifies attacks that compromise availability as Denial of Service attacks. Such attacks may block key signals and affect grid stability and observability. See Lecture 52 (Smart Grid - Part II, slide 17)

11.q: [Week 11] How is the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) described in the lecture?
options: An application of IoT in industries that links automation systems with enterprise, planning, and product lifecycle.
A consumer-only network for home entertainment devices.
A replacement for all industrial automation without networking.
A system used only for storing data without machine communication.
11.solution: IIoT applies IoT concepts to industrial systems and connects automation with enterprise functions, planning, and product lifecycle activities. See Lecture 53 (Industrial Internet of Things - Part I, slide 3)

11.q: [Week 11] Which approach does the lecture associate with IIoT for adapting existing industrial systems?
11.solution: The lecture states that IIoT is based on a 'wrap and re-use' approach rather than a 'rip and replace' approach, allowing existing industrial assets to be integrated. See Lecture 53 (Industrial Internet of Things - Part I, slide 6)

11.q: [Week 11] According to the lecture, which technology is identified as the key enabling technology for vehicle-to-vehicle and vehicle-to-road communications in Intelligent Transportation Systems?
11.solution: The lecture identifies DSRC as the key enabling technology for V2V and V2R communications in connected transportation systems. See Lecture 54 (Industrial Internet of Things - Part II, slide 5)

11.q: [Week 11] In IIoT-based mining applications, which environmental parameters can be monitored using wireless sensor networks?
options: Air quality, poisonous gases, and oxygen level inside mines.
Only the billing amount of mine workers.
Only the color of mining equipment.
Only the internet browsing history of operators.
11.solution: For mining safety, the lecture describes the use of RFID, Wi-Fi, and other wireless technologies for early warning, air-quality monitoring, poisonous-gas detection, and oxygen-level monitoring. See Lecture 54 (Industrial Internet of Things - Part II, slide 7)

11.q: [Week 11] Which Big Data characteristic refers to biases, noise, and abnormality in data?
11.solution: The lecture defines veracity in terms of bias, noise, and abnormality in data and emphasizes its importance for automated decision-making and machine learning. See Lecture 55 (Data Handling and Analytics - Part I, slide 9)

11.q: [Week 11] During data pre-processing, what is the purpose of redundancy mitigation?
options: To prevent data from being collected.
To intentionally duplicate every data item.
To convert all structured data into images.
To eliminate repeated data through detection, filtering, and compression.
11.solution: Redundancy mitigation removes repeated data using detection, filtering, and compression, helping avoid unnecessary transmission and storage. See Lecture 55 (Data Handling and Analytics - Part I, slide 18)

11.q: [Week 11] In Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS), which node stores the actual data blocks?
11.solution: The Namenode maintains filesystem metadata, while Datanodes store the actual data. HDFS divides files into blocks and replicates those blocks across Datanodes. See Lecture 55 (Data Handling and Analytics - Part I, slide 23)

12.q: [Week 12] Which type of data analysis is used for data that is categorical in nature?
12.solution: Qualitative analysis deals with categorical data, whereas quantitative analysis is used for numerical data. See Lecture 56 (Data Handling and Analytics - Part II, slide 3)

12.q: [Week 12] According to the lecture, when is a statistical model classified as a complete model?
options: When the number of variables equals the number of equations
When the model contains no variables
When the number of variables is always greater than the number of equations
When only categorical data are used
12.solution: A complete statistical model has the same number of variables as equations. If these numbers do not match, the model is incomplete. See Lecture 56 (Data Handling and Analytics - Part II, slide 9)

12.q: [Week 12] Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) is best applied when which of the following are to be compared?
options: More than two populations or samples
Only non-numerical labels without any response variable
Only identical copies of the same observation
12.solution: ANOVA is introduced as a parametric statistical technique for comparing datasets and is especially useful when more than two populations or samples are being compared. See Lecture 56 (Data Handling and Analytics - Part II, slide 11)

12.q: [Week 12] What does Pearson's correlation coefficient (r) measure?
options: The number of equations in a statistical model
The maximum value in a dataset
The strength of association between two variables
The sample size of an experiment
12.solution: Pearson's correlation coefficient is used to measure the strength of association between two quantitative, continuous variables. See Lecture 56 (Data Handling and Analytics - Part II, slide 18)

12.q: [Week 12] What is a primary objective of the AgriSens smart water management system?
options: Restricting irrigation control to manual operation only
Increasing irrigation water use regardless of soil condition
Removing all sensors from agricultural fields
Achieving more crop yield with less water
12.solution: AgriSens aims to improve water management by using less water while maintaining or improving crop yield, along with automatic irrigation and remote monitoring. See Lecture 57 (Case Study: Agriculture, slide 4)

12.q: [Week 12] Which set correctly represents the three layers of the proposed AgriSens architecture?
options: Physical layer; transport layer; presentation layer
Sensing and actuating layer; processing, storage and service layer; application layer
User layer; billing layer; routing layer
Sensor layer; firewall layer; operating-system layer
12.solution: The proposed AgriSens architecture is organized into a sensing and actuating layer, a processing, storage and service layer, and an application layer. See Lecture 57 (Case Study: Agriculture, slide 5)

12.q: [Week 12] Which component is included in the integrated design of an AgriSens sensor node?
options: Meter data management system for smart grids
12.solution: The AgriSens sensor node contains sensors and actuators, a processing and memory unit, a wireless communication unit, and a power management unit. See Lecture 57 (Case Study: Agriculture, slide 8)

12.q: [Week 12] What is the function of the multi-user server in the AgriSens remote-server design?
options: It supplies electrical power to the sensor nodes
It measures soil moisture directly in the field
It sends field information to the farmer's mobile phone using SMS and executes farmer queries and control messages
It replaces all gateways with wired links
12.solution: The multi-user server communicates field information to farmers through SMS and also processes farmer queries and control commands. See Lecture 57 (Case Study: Agriculture, slide 10)

12.q: [Week 12] In the IoT healthcare architecture discussed in the lecture, which layer contains smartphones and tablets used as data aggregators?
12.solution: The aggregated layer collects data from sensing-layer devices. Smartphones and tablets are given as examples of aggregators. See Lecture 58 (Case Study: Healthcare, slide 3)

12.q: [Week 12] Which of the following is an example of preventive care enabled by IoT healthcare?
12.solution: The lecture presents fall detection, emergency situation detection, and early anomaly detection as examples of preventive care using IoT healthcare. See Lecture 58 (Case Study: Healthcare, slide 8)

12.q: [Week 12] What is an advantage of continuous activity monitoring?
options: It requires all sensor data to be discarded immediately
It enables daily observation of human behavior and repetitive activity patterns
It can operate only with cameras
12.solution: Continuous monitoring helps observe daily behavior over long periods and identify repetitive patterns that can improve the reliability of activity recognition. See Lecture 59 (Activity Monitoring - Part I, slide 5)

12.q: [Week 12] Which type of data can be analyzed using the deep-learning-based approach described in the lecture?
options: Sensor data only and never images or videos
12.solution: The lecture states that deep-learning-based analysis can be applied to ordinary sensor data as well as image and video data. See Lecture 59 (Activity Monitoring - Part I, slide 8)

12.q: [Week 12] Processing activity-monitoring sensor data directly on the device is referred to as which approach?
12.solution: In the in-place approach, activity data are processed on the device itself. This is generally power intensive but does not require a network connection for the processing task. See Lecture 59 (Activity Monitoring - Part I, slide 9)

12.q: [Week 12] What are the three basic elements used in the smartphone-based activity-monitoring demonstration?
options: A soil-moisture sensor, a pump, and a paddy field
A smart meter, a PMU, and a power plant
A smartphone, a network, and a remote server
A Hadoop Namenode, Datanode, and Job Tracker
12.solution: The demonstration uses a smartphone to generate sensor data, a network to carry the data, and a remote server to receive and process or visualize it. See Lecture 60 (Activity Monitoring - Part II)

12.q: [Week 12] Which sensor values are specifically logged in the activity-monitoring demonstration described in the lecture?
12.solution: For the demonstration, the smartphone transmits accelerometer readings to the remote server, where the data are continuously logged. See Lecture 60 (Activity Monitoring - Part II)
